skill.name: github-multi-repo
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub repositories, package updates, architecture standards, and release workflows with Claude Flow orchestration.
skill.summary: Coordinate multi-repository GitHub work with repository discovery, dependency sync, architecture guidance, and pull request workflows.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Many static matches are Markdown fences or inline documentation and were dismissed as false positives. Several examples do instruct agents to run GitHub CLI, npm, and git commands that can modify many repositories. No prompt injection was found, and the environment variable reference appears to be a benign configuration example.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, a repository allowlist, dry-run output, and rollback instructions before any push or pull request creation.
Use mktemp-created directories, quote variables, validate repository names, and clean up temporary files after each run.
Add warnings and review requirements before writing .github workflows or .claude command files.
Clarify that webhook secrets must stay in approved secret storage and must not be logged or sent to untrusted services.

content.value_statement: Large GitHub organizations struggle to coordinate dependency, architecture, and release changes across many repositories. This skill provides structured multi-repo planning, synchronization, and review workflows.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates multi-repository workflows with Claude Flow swarm patterns.
Discovers GitHub repositories and inspects package dependency files.
Plans package version alignment and documentation synchronization.
Creates branches, commits, and pull requests for coordinated changes.
Guides repository architecture standardization and workflow templates.
Supports dependency, security, health, and reporting workflows.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access and permissions for target repositories.
Example workflows can change repositories, so approval gates are needed.
Does not replace repository security review or branch protection.
Assumes Node.js, npm, and Claude Flow tooling are available.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Service Updates
use_cases.description: Plan dependency or framework updates across related services while preserving test order and pull request visibility.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Structure
use_cases.description: Compare repository layouts, propose shared templates, and align workflows across teams.

use_cases.title: Manage Multi-Package Releases
use_cases.description: Sequence changes across libraries, applications, and documentation with clear ownership and rollout status.

prompt_templates.title: Map Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: List related repositories for my organization and summarize where coordination is needed. Ask before running any commands.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Package Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare package versions across these repositories: <repos>. Identify drift and propose a safe synchronization plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Dependency Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a dependency update plan across <org repos>. Include test order, pull request strategy, rollback steps, and required approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Design Orchestration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-repository orchestration workflow for <program>. Include repository roles, agents, sequencing, risk controls, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Find dependency drift across frontend, backend, and shared repositories.
output: Dependency drift summary grouped by package family.
Recommended update order based on service dependencies.
Pull request plan with tests and rollback checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Plan an organization-wide security patch rollout.
output: Patch sequence with validation steps for each service.
Status report covering completed, blocked, and risky repositories.

output_examples.input: Review architecture standards across three repositories.
output: Common structure gaps and conflicting conventions.
Template recommendations for workflows, documentation, and package metadata.

best_practices: Use dry runs and repository allowlists before making changes.
Keep branch protection, required reviews, and CI checks enabled.
Store credentials in approved secret managers and limit token scopes.
anti_patterns: Running bulk updates without confirming affected repositories.
Using shared temporary paths for concurrent repository jobs.
Disabling tests or branch protection to speed up changes.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate repository discovery, dependency updates, architecture standards, pull requests, and status reporting across GitHub repositories.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows assume GitHub CLI access and permissions for the repositories being inspected or changed.

faq.question: Can it modify repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Several workflows describe branches, commits, pushes, and pull requests, so human approval should be required.

faq.question: Can I use it for read-only planning?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for inventory, comparison, or rollout plans without command execution when you need read-only guidance.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What safeguards should teams use?
faq.answer: Use scoped tokens, repository allowlists, dry runs, branch protection, required reviews, and explicit approval before bulk changes.
